narrative.overview:
MineOps is a focused instrument panel for a player checking a roster between decisions. Dark mode is the locked night-shift control room; light mode translates the same system into bright mineral-paper surfaces for daytime use. Both keep the next action, confidence state, and warning signal unmistakable.

The interface uses survey instruments and control-room readouts without pretending to be a simulator. Dense information is allowed when it is structured; technical provenance stays available but never outranks the player's decision.

rules.name: The Signal-First Rule
rules.body: Teal means act or trust; amber means pause and inspect. Neither accent is decorative.

rules.name: The Two-Workspace Rule
rules.body: Dark mode preserves the night-shift palette exactly. Light mode changes surface and text tones only; signals, hierarchy, spacing, and interaction behavior remain shared.

rules.name: The One Cue Rule
rules.body: A surface uses a border or a shadow as its primary separator. A focused recommendation may use both.

dos: Do lead with the player's next decision.
Do make data confidence and source visible before recommendations.
Do use tactile hover, focus, active, loading, and reduced-motion states.
Do keep technical provenance expandable and subordinate.
donts: Don't flatten light mode into a generic white dashboard.
Don't use teal or amber as decoration without meaning.
Don't make every calculator equally prominent.
Don't use layout-property animation or hide keyboard focus.
